highlights.title: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops
highlights.summary: Microsoft and Nvidia held a launch party for the first wave of RTX Spark laptops last week in San Francisco, where a new wave of AI PCs took center stage amid a packed crowd and a lively hands-on area.
body: One of the biggest challenges was getting Windows ready for AI agents and local AI models. The big selling point of RTX Spark is the combination of Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU, and unified memory to enable powerful AI models to run on a laptop, so the experience of setting up an AI agent needs to be quick and easy.

“When users get into Windows for the first time, they’ll see a new Get Started experience that will launch on an RTX Spark laptop that allows them to find the agent they want, get started with that agent, install it, and get to that agent in only two clicks,” says Peter Dawoud, principal program manager at Microsoft.

Agents can be installed and updated through the Windows Store, so you don’t have to worry about finding updates or figuring out what dependencies each one needs. “We’ll continue to develop it and add more features so that agents can offer a whole new bunch of experiences coming through Windows,” Dawoud says.

highlights.title: MCU Star Teases a Completely New Avengers Project
highlights.summary: The last time we saw Jeremy Renner in the Marvel Cinematic Universe was way back in 2021 in the remarkably charming Hawkeye. Since a second season of the show never materialized, the likelihood of Renner returning to the role of Clint Barton has dwindled dramatically.
body: Renner recently posted a photo on social media showing a set of The West Coast Avengers comic books. The California-based team first appeared in Marvel Comics in 1984 as an offshoot of the Avengers, who operated out of New York. Hawkeye is a founding member, and the team has also included Mockingbird, Wonder Man, Tigra, War Machine and Vision.

A West Coast Avengers project could offer several MCU characters the chance to return. Wonder Man debuted in the MCU just this year in a critically acclaimed series that Disney has since canceled. Paul Betany is currently playing Vision in VisionQuest. The latest incarnation of the West Coast Avengers was led by Kate Bishop, the other Hawkeye who appeared alongside Renner in 2021 played by Hailee Steinfeld. It also included America Chavez, who Xochitl Gomez played in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. It doesn't seem like we are ever actually getting a Young Avengers series, so West Coast Avengers could help fill that void.

body: On Wednesday, the FTC sent out civil investigative demands seeking a wide range of information from the AI firms on recent safety incidents.

The FTC did not respond to Ars’ request to review the subpoena demands. However, Axios’ source said the requests spanned more than 50 pages of questions and sought documents related to the incidents, internal security measures taken, and marketing materials that may suggest consumers were misled.

Soon, third parties targeted by OpenAI and Anthropic agents will also be subpoenaed, Axios’ source said. Any concerning evidence gathered may support FTC litigation, should the FTC decide to sue either or both firms for releasing unsafe products.

OpenAI already faces lawsuits alleging consumer harms, including lawsuits linking its chatbot to matricide, child suicide, school shootings, and other violence. And this week, a group of eight states specifically sued OpenAI over consumer harms, Reuters reported. Like consumers suing, they argued that ChatGPT harms children and “reinforces delusions, encourages dangerous ​behavior, and assists users in planning violence like mass shootings.”

highlights.title: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes
highlights.summary: In hindsight, the post on Instagram should have raised more red flags. The image purported to show actress Mia Goth, just days after filing for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf, posing in a T-shirt with a pointed message: MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN.
body: AI photos and videos of celebrities are racking up millions of views on social media.

It would have been out of character for the star of Pearl, who doesn’t have much of a social media presence, if any. But the Instagram account that posted it, @miagoth_, had more than a million followers and was marked with a blue “verified” checkmark. Within days, the image racked up nearly 500,000 likes, including from peers in the entertainment industry, despite the page being labeled as a fan account.

The image, as The Verge reported, was AI-generated, posted by an account Goth’s representative said they’d complained to Instagram about before for posting “counterfeit, AI images” of Goth. Meta allows users to purchase blue “verified” checkmarks, even if the account is not run by a prominent figure or isn’t an official page.

highlights.title: I’m in my late 60s and in a situationship with a man I really like. I want more but I’m scared of losing him
highlights.summary: Don’t be afraid to speak your desires aloud, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. These are pretty normal, humble things to want. I’m in my late 60s, divorced three years ago.
body: It’s been three months so far, the attraction was instant and strong and felt very promising. We see each other on weekends, which he has stated works for him (partly because he lives an hour away). I’ve told him that I would like to spend more time together and, because of his response, I decided I’d ease off and see what happens. I know he likes me, we get on well and I also know he’s not seeing anyone else. The contact we have in between is sporadic and it’s usually me that initiates it. If he does, it’s very casual. Bottom line – I feel like I’m getting crumbs.

The problem is I’m scared of losing him if I state more definitely what I need. It’s difficult to meet men at my age and, while I have a full and active life, I also crave the intimacy that can only be obtained in a relationship.
Eleanor says: I feel bad for our wants, constantly told they’re overwhelming for other people and pre-emptively ushered from the room.
“They’ll run away if they know what I want” is premised on the idea that your desires are so scary, so pressuring, that even learning about them might be too much for someone.

highlights.title: Singer or clanker? YouTube Music will tell you with new gen AI labeling
highlights.summary: Genuine human creativity takes time, but you know what doesn't? AI slop. There are countless AI models out there that can make something that passes for music, and you might come across those tracks on streaming services without realizing it.
body: Google is not outright banning AI music or even speaking ill of it. “Generative AI is opening up new ways for artists to create, experiment, and share music,” the company says in a blog post.

However, the company also acknowledges that people want to know if a song was created with generative AI tools. A new label for AI content on YouTube Music is now rolling out in the app and on the website, which looks a lot like a label Google began adding to AI-generated videos on YouTube earlier this year.

The AI label will be visible on the player page, and a tap will open a menu with more information. The label will be applied to songs that were created entirely or altered significantly with AI. But how will Google know when to apply that label? That could be a little tricky.

The process of labeling AI music will be similar to Google’s detection setup with YouTube videos. Google says it is working with partners and using its own detection tools to identify AI music. When publishers upload content, they can specify how much (if any) gen AI was used. The tiers are fully gen AI, partially gen AI, and no gen AI. However, this is optional.

There are countless AI models out there that can make something that passes for music, and you might come across those tracks on streaming services without realizing it.

highlights.summary: Rory McIlroy shot a two-under par opening round to finish four shots behind the clubhouse lead on a part-suspended first day of play at the DP World India Championship in New Delhi.
body: McIlroy was midway through the back nine when play was stopped for thunder and lightning in the area, with players then off the course for over four hours.
When play did resume at 4pm local time, McIlroy completed a round of 70 to sit tied 13th.
The world No 2 started from the par-four 10th, which he bogeyed, and went out in 34 after birdies at the 13th, 15th and 18th.
He found another birdie at the second hole but followed that with a second bogey of the round at the third, before finishing with six successive pars.

body: “I obviously was drawn to the script, but didn’t immediately think, ‘This is my next project,'” Morrison tells Variety over Zoom. “It really was just, this is good writing and I want to talk about it with this writer.”

Morrison and Cox really connected. “There was a deep sense of mutual respect, but also, for this script that was incredibly well received and jumped off the page, she was not precious about it,” Morrison says. “The more I sat with it, the more it sort of got under my skin.”

The same was true for the film’s cast, an all-star ensemble led by Margaret Qualley as Maya and including Gabriel Basso as Charlie; Aaron Pierre as Felix, a handsome stranger she meets abroad; Patrick Schwarzenegger as her best friend Jason; and Catherine Keener in a scene-stealing performance as Charlie’s mother Ruth.
“We have leading actors playing supporting roles, and I think that’s because this really spoke to them,” Morrison says.

highlights.title: Rewilding could help vulnerable islands keep pace with rising seas
highlights.summary: Coral-fringed tropical atolls are among the landforms most threatened by global warming, but many have a potential superpower: Healthy ecosystems may help them keep pace with rising seas.
body: Atoll islands with native vegetation and thriving seabird populations are “naturally active systems that can change and adapt to their environmental conditions if they are allowed to do so,” said Nick Graham, a marine ecologist at Lancaster University in the United Kingdom, who led an international team of scientists that studied island resilience across 28 atoll islands in the Pacific and Indian oceans.

Their paper, published Wednesday in Science Advances, shows that restoring atoll ecosystems reinforces their growth. Seabirds ferry nutrients from the open ocean and deposit them on the atolls as guano that nurtures land plants, marine life and coral growth. This provides more material for reef building, as parrotfish and other reef feeders turn dead coral into sand to maintain beaches, while native plants with extensive root networks stabilize sediments.

Eradicating rats and replacing coconut plantations with native forests and brush could give some atolls a “fighting chance” to persist at the rate of sea-level rise expected toward the end of the century with about 2° Celsius (3.6° Fahrenheit) of warming, Graham said.

highlights.title: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
highlights.summary: There's a new digital pet in town - a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to "Eiliko" over Wi-Fi, it'll phone home to China.
body: Eiliko and its manufacturer, Energize Lab, are seemingly not to be trusted.
I bought an Eiliko from Amazon on August 29th. During a 10-minute conversation on August 30th, I asked the little bot: “Do you ever tell anybody else what I’m saying?”
Within minutes, a man on the other side of the planet had a complete transcript of everything I’d told the toy.

He didn’t just have my conversations, either. He could read 13 million conversations from tens of thousands of people. He could access seemingly the entire active worldwide fleet of 68,000 robot toys. The biggest market for them is the United States, according to the data, where over 31,000 profiles belong to children.

This date is close to last year’s cutoff of Nov. 21, 2025. To be eligible for the Player’s Voice category (the fan vote), games must ship on or before Nov. 30. GTA 6 releases at Nov. 19, so it gets in just under the wire.

Game industry insider NateTheHate recently claimed that Rockstar is sending critics review codes before the end of October, which would give judges ample time to play the game before they cast their votes. Last year, nominees for the 2025 Game Awards were announced on Nov. 17, four days before the cutoff. If Rockstar delays sending out codes because it's concerned about leaks, the judges would have very little time to decide whether it should be Game of the Year.

highlights.title: Supercell confirms Squad Busters will shut down on December 14
highlights.summary: Supercell has confirmed Squad Busters will be removed from the App Store and Google Play on December 1 and stop being playable on December 14. The developer said players who already have the game installed can keep playing until December 14, with all events and timers ending on that date.
body: Supercell announced the end of Squad Busters development last October, stating that it expected to close the game at some point in 2026. In-app purchases have been switched off since then, and the window to transfer purchase value to other Supercell games closed at the end of 2025.
The developer said it could not see “a clear path forward” for the game after several reworks, including its Heroes update. It said further changes would have made it almost a completely new game.

Squad Busters launched worldwide in May 2024. AppMagic estimates put its lifetime revenue at about $67.9m from 58.6m downloads, with the US accounting for 30% of spending. That works out at an estimated $1.16 in revenue per download globally.
The company has also ruled out offline play, private servers and releasing the code, saying the game contains content and characters from across its other titles.

highlights.summary: “La Bola Negra” soundtrack, featuring music by composer Raül Refree, is set to be released on Oct. 16 by Lakeshore Records. Taking its name from an unfinished play by Lorca and drawing on his writings and legacy, “La Bola Negra” is directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi better known as Los…
body: It’s an intense score that grows along with the film and with the different protagonists as their stories unfold.

Refree, who is one of Variety’s 10 artisans to watch, tied his instrumentation to the characters rather than the eras. “Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) plays the trumpet, so his scenes rely heavily on the brass section. Carlos (Milo Quifes) plays the piano, so his music features the piano alongside the string section. Finally, Alberto’s (González) story takes place in the present day, and because he is going through a personal crisis, his music relies much more on silence,” Refree says.

As the film progresses and the paths of the three protagonists cross in one way or another, the timbres and instrumental approach also begin to blend. “Mira que nos acechan” is where all the concepts come together, carrying the meaning that we are all one.

highlights.title: Sedimentary rocks: why pét nat and cloudy wines are on the rise
highlights.summary: There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection … Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”.
body: So why choose a cloudy or unfiltered wine? “There’s texture, there’s fleshiness, there’s rounded fruit,” says Zainab Majerikova, head of wine for the Ottolenghi group, where the three house wines are unfiltered and cloudy natural numbers. “We think this makes them more moreish and a better fit for food with big, complex flavours,” says Majerikova.

I always get the sense that longer contact with lees (those dead yeast cells) makes cloudy wine more food-like; it might be a drink, but there’s a crunchiness to it. For the full effect of its flavours and weight on the palate, Majerikova recommends shaking a bottle of cloudy wine before opening to mix the sediment with the liquid. Either way, she says, cloudiness “brings soul, vibrancy and complexity” to wines for old-fashioned fun.

Alma 4 Phos Pét Nat £12 Tesco, 12.5%. Food-versatile pét nat Argentinian chardonnay from the Uco Valley, lightly sparkling and textural.

highlights.title: Cult venue Prince Charles cinema ‘saved’ after lease renewal signed
highlights.summary: The much-loved central London institution, which has been threatened with closure since January 2025, secures 25-year lease without break clause with current landlords.
body: The celebrated Prince Charles repertory cinema in London’s Leicester Square has announced that the threat of closure has been staved off by signing a new 25-year lease with its landlords.

In a post on social media titled “You Saved the PCC”, the cinema said that “after 21 months of uncertainty, we’re delighted to have secured the future of the cinema” and that they had “signed a new 25-year lease with no break clause, ensuring our projectors will keep rolling for years to come”.
The cinema also expressed its gratitude for the “support, commitment and belief of many, many people”.

In January 2025, the Prince Charles launched a petition, claiming that its landlord, Zedwell LSQ Ltd (owned by developer Criterion Capital) was trying to “bully us out of the building” by demanding a break clause in its lease, due for renewal in September 2025. The break clause would have enabled Zedwell to give the cinema six months’ notice if it had other plans for the site. At the time, Criterion Capital denied that it was attempting to intimidate or disadvantage the cinema.

highlights.title: Microsoft’s new Photos app combines your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud galleries
highlights.summary: Microsoft has redesigned its Photos app for Windows 11, overhauling the editor and image viewer, and combining photos and videos from your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud into a single space.
body: To combine your galleries in the Windows 11 Photos app, you’ll need to turn on Camera Backup in the OneDrive mobile app on iOS or Android, and follow Apple’s guide to set up iCloud for Windows. Once combined in the Windows 11 Photos app, you can browse by date, organize and share albums, search for specific photos via descriptions or by the people featured in them, and more. You can browse files online or offline, and Microsoft says photos will be available on your device “even when you’re not connected.”

The new Photos editor has been “rebuilt from the ground up,” according to Microsoft, launching 25 percent faster and arranging tools into four categories: Crop, Enhance, Repair, and Stylize. The Photos app now also preserves HDR quality during editing processes and allows you to edit and save HEIC and WebP images without altering their original format.

highlights.title: Gen Z wrestle with shame from ordering delivery food: ‘This economy is not for the weak’
highlights.summary: As Americans use apps like DoorDash and Uber Eats more habitually, they confront the guilt of paying extra fees for convenience. When it comes to food, Caroline Bauldree does not like to “deprive” herself of anything. She does not like to cook either, so that means a lot of food deliveries.
body: Bauldree got into the habit of near-daily DoorDashing back in college. “I could order whatever food from whatever restaurant and it showed up at my door – that’s the dream,” she said. “But then I just feel like crap about myself because I’m like, ‘wow, I’m a lazy piece of shit.’ Nine times out of 10, I feel bad about myself.”

There is a term for that post-order clarity: delivery guilt. The pandemic turned food delivery apps such as DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub, once only popular in major cities, into a full-fledged national lifestyle. One Purdue study found that two-thirds of consumers used a food-ordering app at least once in 2024; another recent survey from the marketing company FinanceBuzz in partnership with Bank of America found that 57% of Americans get takeout or delivery weekly or more. Gen Z is more likely to feed the habit, clocking in an average of five orders a month – roughly double the monthly orders made by Boomers.

Leoni, a £26m signing from Parma in 2025, sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury against Southampton 13 months ago. Iraola has disclosed the damage extended beyond the ACL and Liverpool must tread carefully with the 19-year-old’s rehabilitation as a consequence.

“It is taking more time than we wanted,” the head coach said. “With Gio, the plan was to train with the team in this past international break. It is probably now going to be the next international break [which starts on 9 November], so we have lost one month in the process.

highlights.title: Ralph Fiennes to Star In, Executive Produce ‘Unbeaten’ Racehorse Drama for ‘Conclave’ Producer, StudioCanal
highlights.summary: He will play Sir Henry Cecil, the legendary horse trainer, with 'Outrun' director Nora Fingscheidt to helm the theatrical feature set to shoot in 2027.
body: Ralph Fiennes is set to star in and executive produce Unbeaten, a theatrical feature from Conclave producer House Productions, StudioCanal and Escapade Pictures.

The theatrical feature in advanced development is based on screenplay by Bash Doran and will be directed by BAFTA winner Nora Fingscheidt ( Outrun ). “I knew nothing about the legendary Henry Cecil until I read Bash Doran’s screenplay. I was compelled and moved by it and by Henry’s story with the great horse Frankel. Henry was — and still is — a unique figure, complex and competitive in the very specific world of horse racing,” Fiennes, who received an Oscar nomination for his performance in Edward Berger’s Vatican-set drama. said in a statement.
His other credits include Wuthering Heights, Quiz Show, The English Patient, Schindler’s List, In Bruges, The Grand Budapest Hotel and The Menu.

The film reunites Fiennes with House Productions’ Tessa Ross, who also produced Conclave. Rory Aitken of Escapade Pictures and 42 will also produce. StudioCanal is fully financing the project, handling worldwide sales and is set to release Unbeaten in the U.K., France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Benelux, Australia and New Zealand.

highlights.title: Bottega Veneta Took Over the Guggenheim for Taryn Simon’s Big Night
highlights.summary: Bottega Veneta gathered friends of the house at the Guggenheim to experience Father Country I Do Love You, multidisciplinary artist Taryn Simon’s monumental, decade-long undertaking, presented against the backdrop of the nation’s 250th birthday.
body: “It’s like a birth,” Simon said, describing the whirlwind of finally presenting the project. “I’m in a daze.” With a procession of admirers approaching her all evening, fresh from exploring the works and eager to share their impressions, there was hardly a second for her to catch her breath. Simon’s summation of it all? “There’s lots of blood. And exhaustion. Amazement, blood, and exhaustion.” As if on cue, novelist Salman Rushdie swept her into a long hug, followed by performance artist Marina Abramović.

The show marks both the first monographic exhibition by a photography-based artist in the museum’s rotunda and the largest debut of new work ever staged at the Guggenheim. Across 42 multipart artworks, which Simon calls “chapters,” she follows the real life of an unnamed federal agent, tracing the consequences of his actions and inactions through photographs, text, videos, and sculptures. “Oh my God! It’s just breathtaking,” exclaimed Julianne Moore in response to the exhibit. “I’m such a huge fan of Taryn’s. She’s an extraordinary artist, and what she manages to do in this show… she physicalizes a feeling, and does it in terms of personal relationships and lived lives.”
